title: ActiveRecord: relation first, SQL later
outcome: Predict query timing and repair N+1 without loading every association.
book: Metaprogramming Ruby ch. 9: ActiveRecord as a DSL
cue: Build the query. Ask for rows. Count the SQL.

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A list uses Task.all.to_a.select { |t| !t.done }.first(20), then reads every owner. Repair both the row loading and association problem.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: A dashboard needs a count of completed tasks per project. Should you load all tasks and count in Ruby?

trace.title: where and order
trace.detail: An ActiveRecord relation is a description of a query. where, order, and limit can build it. Iteration often executes it. Once you call to_a, later filtering is usually Ruby work over loaded rows.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Draw the relation-building calls before the first SQL. Then draw the initial task query and the association-loading query. With a simple belongs_to preload, adding more tasks should not add one owner query per task.

Compare one task and twenty tasks. Confirm the response needs each loaded field. An association cache on already loaded objects can make a repeated access look cheap; start the measurement with fresh records.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: Calling size, count, and length can have different SQL behavior depending on loaded state. A Ruby block passed to select after loading does not become a SQL WHERE clause.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Predict query timing and repair N+1 without loading every association. Give a concrete failure example.
